fields.h1: Build a LinkedIn Landing Page for Every Ad, Profile, and Post
fields.hero_description: Build a LinkedIn landing page that tags each lead with the ad or post it came from, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Where a LinkedIn Click Lands and What It Saves
fields.features_subheading: A LinkedIn landing page is the page a click on an ad, a profile link, or a post opens. Emergent builds it and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
A page for each ad, from one prompt

Describe the offer and the people the ad targets, and Emergent builds the page with its form and the table behind it. A second ad that needs a new headline takes one more prompt.
fields.feature_2:
The ad's tag stays with each lead

The app reads the UTM values in the link that opened the page and saves them on the lead's row. Count leads by ad or by campaign straight from that table, with no spreadsheet merge.
fields.feature_3:
Answers decide who follows up

Set a rule on any answer, such as company size or job title, and the app emails the person who owns that kind of lead. A Slack alert to a shared channel works the same way.
fields.feature_4:
New leads reach the CRM you already use

The app connects to HubSpot or any other tool with an API and sends each new lead there with its answers and its tag. Sales sees the lead without waiting on a weekly export.
fields.feature_5:
Every lead lives in a database you own

Each submission is a row in a database that belongs to you rather than a rented form inbox. Filter it by campaign, or point a dashboard at it when the quarterly review comes up.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes to GitHub on paid plans

Export the page and its database code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own stack or extend it later, without rebuilding the page from zero.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a LinkedIn Click Starts
fields.tab_content_1:
Three ads, one page, and 412 requests sorted by ad

Halvard Freight Data runs three Sponsored Content ads that all point to one page offering its 2026 freight rate report. Each request is saved with the ad's tag from the link. Of last month's 412 requests, the carrier map ad brought 214, the quote chart ad 131, and the text-only ad 67.
fields.tab_content_2:
Companies at $5M or more get the longer call

Odile Marchetti, a fractional CFO, keeps one link in her profile's Featured section: a call request page that asks for annual revenue. A company at $5M or more is offered a 45-minute call, and a smaller one gets a 20-minute intro. Every request is saved to her calls table.
fields.tab_content_3:
Joel Amari takes every demo for 50 trucks or more

Visitors who click the custom button on Corvane Fleet's company Page land on a demo request page that asks for fleet size. A request for 50 trucks or more, such as Dunmore Haulage with 120, is emailed to account executive Joel Amari. Smaller fleets get a recorded walkthrough by email.
fields.tab_content_4:
One post sent 186 people to a payroll calculator

Ines Varga, who founded Pellridge Payroll, ended a post with a link to a savings calculator. It multiplies a company's hourly staff by 6 minutes saved per pay run. In the 5 days after the post, 186 visitors ran it and 41 asked for the full breakdown by email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a LinkedIn Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a LinkedIn landing page that matches its ad and saves each lead with the link that sent it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Repeat the promise in the ad
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only for what the follow-up needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the LinkedIn surface this page serves: a Sponsored Content ad, the Featured section of a profile, a company Page button, or a post. Each one brings a visitor with a different question in mind. Give each its own page instead of one page for all four.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The visitor clicked on one specific promise, such as a freight rate report or a 45-minute call. Put that promise in the headline in the same words where you can, and keep the first screen to that one offer and its form.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the fields the person who follows up will use, such as company name, annual revenue, or fleet size, and cut the rest. Every extra field is one more thing a visitor types before the page has earned it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write one prompt with the offer and the rule for each answer, for example who gets an email when a company passes a size. Emergent turns that prompt into the page and the database it saves to, ready to review before anything goes live.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Tag every link before it goes live
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add UTM values to the URL in each ad or post, one value per ad, and the app saves them on each lead's row. LinkedIn's dynamic UTM tracking can add tracking parameters to the landing page URLs of your ad creatives for you.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the CRM and the alerts
fields.howto_step_6_des: Map each lead's answers and its ad tag to fields in your CRM, and set an email or Slack alert for leads that need a person the same day. Then check that the tag shows up on the CRM record next to the answers.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the page from the LinkedIn ad preview or your own profile link before anyone else does. Submit one test lead, check that its row carries the right tag, and confirm the alert reached the right person before the campaign starts.

faq_plan.q: What is a LinkedIn landing page?
faq_plan.a: A LinkedIn landing page is a web page made for visitors who click through from LinkedIn, whether the link sat in a sponsored ad, a member's profile, a company Page, or someone's post. Unlike a homepage, it has one offer and one form, and the offer matches the click.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a LinkedIn landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the offer and what should happen to each lead in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the page and the database table behind it. Add a UTM value to each LinkedIn link, send one test lead, and publish.

faq_plan.q: What do the best LinkedIn landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: Look for two things in any LinkedIn landing page example: a headline that repeats the ad's offer in the same words, and a form short enough to finish in under a minute. Then check what the page offers a visitor who is not ready to buy, such as a recorded walkthrough instead of a sales call.

faq_plan.q: Should LinkedIn landing pages be different from pages for other channels?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Write LinkedIn landing pages for the job titles and company sizes your ad targets, and ask for work details such as company name and team size. Partner traffic needs its own page: an affiliate landing page carries the partner's offer and tracking link instead. Emergent builds each version from its own prompt.

faq_plan.q: When does a LinkedIn landing page beat a lead gen form?
faq_plan.a: A landing page wins when the visitor needs to see more before signing up, or when you want the answers in your own table. A Lead Gen Form wins when speed matters more. LinkedIn's Lead Gen Forms automatically fill in member profile information matched to the ad set's targeting.

faq_plan.q: How does a LinkedIn landing page record which ad sent each lead?
faq_plan.a: Through a UTM value. Give each ad its own value in its destination URL, and the page stores that value with the lead. With LinkedIn's Insight Tag installed on the page, page load conversions are counted when LinkedIn member accounts visit it, which gives you a second count to check against your table.

faq_plan.q: Can a LinkedIn landing page double as the page for search ads?
faq_plan.a: It can, but separate pages read better. A search visitor typed a query, and a ppc landing page repeats that query back; a LinkedIn visitor saw an offer in the feed, and the page should repeat the ad. Emergent can build both from one prompt and keep their leads in the same database, tagged by source.

faq_plan.q: Can I link a LinkedIn landing page from my own profile?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Link the one page you most want profile visitors to act on, such as a call request or a report. LinkedIn's Featured section can hold links to external websites, for example your personal blog or portfolio, and a landing page link works the same way. Tag it with its own UTM value to keep those leads apart from ad leads.

faq_plan.q: How many form fields should a LinkedIn landing page ask for?
faq_plan.a: Start with 3: name, work email, and the one answer that decides the follow-up, such as company size or annual revenue. Add a field only when someone will act on it within a day. With Emergent, every answer is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should a LinkedIn landing page show up in search results?
faq_plan.a: Only the evergreen version should. Keep ad variants out of search: a noindex rule is used to prevent indexing content by search engines that support the rule. The evergreen page then follows ordinary landing page seo practice, with a clear title and copy that answers a real search.

plan.angle: The SERP for this keyword is LinkedIn's own help pages and ad guides plus example roundups; none shows the page behind the click being built, or what happens to the person who fills it in. This page shows four LinkedIn landing pages built from a prompt, one per place a LinkedIn click starts: a Sponsored Content ad, the Featured section of a profile, the custom button on a company Page and a founder's post. Each tab follows the click to where it lands: a lead tagged with its ad, a call length set by revenue, a demo request routed by fleet size, a calculator result emailed on request. The FAQ covers the definition, examples, landing page versus Lead Gen Form, tracking by ad, the Featured link, field count and search indexing, every LinkedIn fact quoted from LinkedIn's own documentation.
